static_read_responses.barrow_marker_stone: The lichen-sunk stone reads: HERE KEEP FAITH WITH THE OLD FIELD. DISTURB NOTHING. LIGHT YOUR LANTERN. LEAVE BEFORE THE LAST BELL. One lower name strip has worked loose, and the dirt beneath it is cleaner than the grave around it should allow.
static_read_responses.barrow_votive_ring: Most of the chapel candles died normally. The ones nearest the dais have wax trails climbing the stone against gravity, each thread pointing toward Edric's slab like a finger that lost patience.
static_read_responses.blackreed_standard: A black marsh reed is stitched over a split road line. Not heraldry. A toll notice in cloth, declaring who gets to pass beneath this hill and who gets left in the rain.
static_read_responses.blackwater_lens_frame: The lens frame is bent around a cold white core like the brass tried to hold the light in place and learned too late that it was the part being reshaped instead.
static_read_responses.boglight_lantern: The lantern cage is cold, but something pale still clings to the green glass from the inside. One scratched note on the hook reads: IF IT LOOKS LIKE A GUIDE LIGHT, IT ISN'T.
static_read_responses.carrion_stake_circle: Most of the stakes were hammered by anxious human hands. The newer cuts across them were not. A crow skull has been tied to the tallest one with reed cord and black bog thread.
static_read_responses.cellar_warning_slate: Uncle Pib's chalk scrawl reads: IF YOU ARE HOLDING THIS SLATE, THE RATS HAVE NOT EATEN YOU. GOOD. CLEAR THEM OUT BEFORE THEY RUIN THE STORES. IF THE ROAD STAYS CUT, FLOUR BECOMES STRATEGIC.
static_read_responses.dawn_bell: The bell's bronze lip is etched with a prayer worn soft by generations of hands: LET MORNING FIND US, LET MEMORY REST, LET THE LOST HEAR THE WAY HOME. Those who kneel beneath it before a hard road still say the chapel answers. Pray if you mean to test that.
static_read_responses.drifted_reed_tags: Mira's survey knots are clean and identical, but the tags sit at three different heights. The reeds did not grow that way overnight. Something moved the marks without using the mud.
static_read_responses.drowned_survey_marker: The old survey cut reads: SOUTH WEIR LINE / BLACKWATER FEED / LAMP HOUSE EAST. A newer scratch over it is less official and more useful: IF THE LIGHT IS STILL BURNING, TURN IT WRONGER OR TURN IT OFF.
static_read_responses.edrics_slab: The cracked slab still carries a knightly carving beneath the moss: SIR EDRIC VALE, WHO HELD THE LINE UNTIL THE LINE OUTLIVED HIM.
static_read_responses.family_post_sign: The sign names the family post as a rally point for new hands, visiting kin, and anyone still learning which gate leads to work and which gate leads to trouble.
static_read_responses.feast_hall_cauldron: The cauldron holds a stew thick with bone broth, scavenged roots, and the sort of meat nobody decent should identify after the first guess.
static_read_responses.fenreach_waypost: The old road mark once pointed to a survey line no one in Brambleford still uses. A newer charcoal warning cuts across it in Mira's hand: BLACKFEN SOUTH. KEEP TO THE HARD GROUND UNTIL THE MARSH STOPS LYING.
static_read_responses.forge_order_board: Torren's board reads: NAIL KEGS FOR SOUTH FARM. HINGE SET FOR MAYOR'S HALL. TWO SPEAR TIPS FOR THE WATCH. Below that, in heavier chalk: FIELD KIT IMPROVEMENTS DONE TO ORDER. WEAR IT IN. BRING SCRAP. PAY SILVER. ASK AT THE FORGE, NOT WITH STORIES.
static_read_responses.great_catch_log: Most entries are fish weights, weather complaints, and proud exaggerations. The newest note is different: pale light seen south of the reeds, no bite on the line, went home early.
static_read_responses.hunters_warning_post: Three deep knife-cuts have been carved into the cedar, then crossed out beneath a newer line: GREYMAW TOOK THE OUTER TRAIL. STAY IN NUMBERS.
static_read_responses.kitchen_hearth: The hearth stones are warm, scrubbed, and ringed with little reminders: keep soup low, dry herbs high, and never waste a clean flame when the town may need it after dark.
static_read_responses.loaner_pole_rack: Each pole has a tag, a nicked cork grip, and a warning from Uncle Pib: borrowed tackle comes back cleaner than it left or it starts telling stories about you.
static_read_responses.lower_lanternworks_notice: The notice is written in Joss's exact hand: Lower Lanternworks open for inspection. Do not touch south-line glass without Joss Veller present. Someone has added: this includes tapping.
static_read_responses.lower_lanternworks_plaque: The plaque is a maintenance map for Brambleford's road lanterns. North, west, and town lines are cold. The south groove is stained dark and faintly warm.
static_read_responses.mayors_ledger: The open ledger carries three fresh entries in the mayor's square hand: LANTERN OIL SHORT BY TWO CRATES. WEST WATCH REPORTS LIGHT LOSS AT DUSK. CHAPEL REQUESTS ADDITIONAL VOLUNTEERS WITH STEADY NERVES.
static_read_responses.midden_bone_totem: The totem is wired together from feast scraps, old threats, and small bones polished by handling. Three scratched signs circle the lid-face: KING, POT, ROAD. Repetition does not make them wiser.
static_read_responses.miretooth_shed_skull: The skull is too heavy through the jaw and too narrow through the eyes to belong to anything Brambleford would name kindly. Deep score marks along the bone suggest the beast that shed it grew into something even worse.
static_read_responses.moonleaf_warning_ribbon: Maybelle's ribbon marks the moonleaf cleanly, but the plants lean hard away from the old barrow route. Someone has added one nervous chalk word on the back of the tag: LISTEN.
static_read_responses.numbered_signal_arrows: The signal arrows are marked with route numbers and short notches for distance. Blackreed's archers were not only hunting travelers; they were measuring which roads could still answer each other.
static_read_responses.old_fence_cut_tally: The tally counts twelve missing rails, five clean axe cuts, and two wagon plank marks. Mira's last line is short: RUK DID NOT CUT RANDOMLY.
static_read_responses.outfitters_chalkboard: Leda's chalk hand is spare and direct: WE BUY PELTS, HERBS, SALVAGE, ROAD SCRAP, AND OTHER SENSIBLE FINDS. FAIR PRICES FOR FAIR HANDS. ASK ABOUT A SHIFT IF YOU WANT TO EARN THE BETTER COLUMN.
static_read_responses.potking_lid_throne: The throne has accumulated more than it was built. Pot lids, road shields, and dented signboards have been hammered into a seat that mistakes noise for wealth and grease for polish.
static_read_responses.ruks_chopping_block: Fresh cuts score the block in harsh, uneven lines. One gouge has been hacked deep enough to lodge a shred of wagon paint and a few pale flecks of lantern glass. A goblin hand has scratched nearby: RUK KEEPS THIS ROAD.
static_read_responses.signal_brazier: Fresh soot rims the iron pan, and the stacked wood beside it has been sorted into quick-burn bundles. The tower crew means to signal far and fast if the ridge turns ugly.
static_read_responses.sinkmouth_scratch_map: The slate shows a goblin scratch map: CAMP crossed out, then arrows leading east into a crown mark over a grease-slick room. One soot-smeared note is clearer than the rest: POT-KING EATS FIRST.
static_read_responses.sludge_run_flour_sack: The sack still bears Uncle Pib's flour mark under the sludge. A goblin has scratched a pot symbol beside it, as if stolen food becomes official once it is ugly enough.
static_read_responses.sluice_work_order_plate: The stamped plate reads: SOUTH LINE / SLUICE WALK / ORDER COILBACK-7. The last digit has been cut deeper than the others, renewed again and again after rust tried to close it.
static_read_responses.star_lens: The etched brass rings mark stars, road lines, and old service routes around Brambleford. The Nexus marks are dark, locked behind a brass seal that has not answered Joss in years.
static_read_responses.sunken_lock_chain: The chain hums through the black water in time with the wrong light overhead. Someone once stamped the nearest link with a warning that still survives the rust: DO NOT DRAW FULL LINE WITHOUT LAMP-HOUSE ORDER.
static_read_responses.town_notice_board: Town notices crowd the board in practical layers: road crews needed east of the gate, chapel candles to be saved for dusk, and a fresh line from Mayor Elric asking everyone to report bad lanterns before they become worse roads.
static_read_responses.trophy_vitrine: Glass cases hold the proof of Act 1 wins: Miretooth's Fen Jaw, the Blackreed Battle Standard, the Pot-King's Battered Lid, the Blackwater Beacon Core, and the white-black Hollow Lantern Prism. The newest label is still clean enough to catch the lanternlight: SOUTH LINE DARK, FIRST CHAPTER CLOSED.
static_read_responses.tutorial_damaged_cart: The cart axle is split clean through, but the chalk marks beside it are instructional: brace the load, check the wheel pin, then call for help before a small mistake becomes a road problem.
static_read_responses.tutorial_supply_board: Quartermaster notes list loaner gear, bandage counts, and the rule written twice in darker chalk: take what keeps you alive, return what keeps the next person alive too.
static_read_responses.watchtower_warning_post: The old carving reads: BORDER WATCH POST THREE. KEEP FIRE LOW. SIGNAL SOUTH IF THE RIDGE MOVES. Someone newer has cut a reply beneath it: TOO LATE FOR THAT.
static_read_responses.weir_keepers_plaque: The greened plaque reads: KEEP SOUTH LIGHT TRIMMED. HOLD THE LOCK LINE. MAINTAIN NIGHT SIGNAL FOR BRAMBLEFORD APPROACH. The words are ordinary civic orders. The wet brass around them is not.
static_read_responses.woods_wardstone: The chalk marks are fresh enough to smear under a thumb. Beneath the warning DO NOT FOLLOW THE QUIET, an older cut mark faces west toward the barrow route: a boundary sign, not a prayer. Someone has recently rubbed charcoal over it and stopped before the line could flake away.

brother_alden.text: "Wax does not climb stone unless something is answering from beneath it. The votive ring gives the chapel a direction, and direction is better than dread."

"The old field is not waking as an army. That would be simpler and worse in a more honest way. Start at Marker Row, find the loose name, and see whether the circle beyond it has begun answering. Bring me proof before I turn fear into prayer and call it wisdom."

"A name is a small mercy, but it is still mercy. I can put this back in the chapel record and stop calling that grave an it. If Sir Edric is stirring deeper in the field, we go to him with names in our mouths, not just weapons in our hands."
"Before you take the road, carry a little order with you. The Dawn Bell is only bronze, but the town hears steadier footsteps when someone remembers to light a candle and check on the frightened."

"Sir Edric lies at the Sunken Dais, but not quietly enough. When grave-lights answer him, cut those lesser spirits down first. The ward around him should fail once the dead he leans on are gone. Ring the Dawn Bell and pray before you cross if you want steadier hands."

"The causeway is fouled and the circle beyond it is waking. Go into Old Barrow Field, put down four of the restless dead, and return only if the silence starts to sound honest again. Take the bell's blessing with you first if you have any sense."

"The Dawn Bell has started answering with a thin, wrong note at dusk. Cross the causeway and see whether the field itself is stirring. If the air turns cold and the crows stop making natural noises, trust that instinct. And if you mean to go, pray before you leave the chapel."
"The bell rings clean again. That is not peace, exactly, but it is close enough for town sleep and chapel thanks."

"The Dawn Bell sounded once at dusk without shaking. I know that sounds small after a drowned lamp house and a thing made of wrong light, but small mercies are still the way a town learns it survived."

"The chapel keeps records, candles, and the sort of silence people only notice when they lose it. If you need the Dawn Bell at your back before a hard road, ring your courage true and pray here before you leave."

captain_harl_rowan.text: "Numbered arrows mean command work. Blackreed was measuring roads, not just firing from them. That turns a robbery problem into a position problem. Good find."

"Blackreed is not just robbing wagons if he has the old tower organized. Get to the ledge, check the breach yard, and bring me anything that reads like a count. A thief takes. A commander sorts first."
"This is not a loot list. It is a route map with prices attached to people. Good find. Now we know Blackreed meant to own the ridge, not haunt it. That makes finishing him less optional."

"Then this one is about finishing the line, not scouting it. Joss has the drowned works in his head better than I do, but the tactical answer is simple: if that lamp thing leans on lesser bodies, clear those first and break its footing before you try to end the room."

"Good. Short route, bad footing, wrong light. That is a capstone. Clear the drowned lock crews, keep the party inside shouting distance, and keep watch on anyone tempted to trade formation for one clever angle."
"Miretooth was teeth. If Joss says the south light itself is wrong, believe the part where the problem got less animal and more deliberate. Hit the weir cleanly and report back with something final."

"Good. First real work stays inside town walls because stores matter if the road stays cut. Head south, read the board if you want the damage written twice, then go west to the inn and talk to Uncle Pib. Clear his cellar before you chase the black lantern."

"Then end it. If Mira says the fen beast has started treating the marsh like a border, believe her. Hit hard, stay together, and don't chase anything that disappears into reeds unless the whole party means it."
"Good. The south fen path is real trouble, not rumor. Chart the rise, thin whatever's hunting that marsh edge, and come back with a cleaner count than the crows would leave."
"South of the old camp the ground turns into bad marsh and worse visibility. Get eyes on it for Mira and don't let the first quiet stretch convince you the fen's empty."

"Then finish the warrens cleanly. The feast hall is where goblins get loud, but the crown room beyond it is where Grubnak keeps their nerve from leaking out. Hit the court hard and don't give his helpers time to turn the cave into a dogpile."
"The road problem wasn't just bandits. The goblins have a whole filth hole under Ruk's old camp. Thin the warrens crews before they remember how close Brambleford sits."

"Blackreed's papers and Mira's tracks point to a sink cut east of the old camp. Find it, get eyes on how deep the warrens run, and don't let the first tunnel fool you into thinking the goblins are disorganized down there."
"Blackreed wins by seeing weakness before decent folk do. Take the climb, clear the line around him, and don't let him pick off whoever looks closest to folding."
"The ledge and the stairs are the real fight. Push north from Ruk's old camp, clear the archers first if they start ruling the pace, and don't let the hounds split the party."
"The old tower sits north of Fencebreaker Camp. Get eyes on the approach and the breach yard, then come back if you somehow discover they are polite visitors."

"There you are. Tamsin says you can stand, so now we find out whether you can help. The south lantern is out and the road cart came in torn, but first we keep town food from becoming rat confetti. Check your gear, then head south to the green and west to Uncle Pib."

"Ruk's the first name tied to the cut rails, the stolen planks, and maybe that dead south lantern. He punishes anyone foolish enough to face him alone. Gather the family if you need to, then hit him together."

"Town's done teaching you what it can. The cart mud, claw marks, and cut harness all point east. Head for Mira at the gate, keep the party together, and check your map if you want the road laid out before you push."
"If the goblins are still cutting fences, press to the Old Fence Line and Wolf Turn. Those rails kept homes standing yesterday. Today they are pointing us at whoever wanted the road open and dark."

"That is a chapter worth of trouble dealt with: road, woods, barrows, ridge, warrens, fen, and now the south light itself. Good. Go put that prism in the hall upstairs and let the town breathe for one evening."
"The Beacon Core is a heavy piece of work, but it belongs in the vitrine. One less hinge for the weir to turn on."
"Blackreed learned that the ridge doesn't belong to whoever talks loudest. His standard is in the hall now, and the road's open."
"Grubnak was a king of junk, but he was still a king. Ending that court in the warrens was a clean piece of work. Put the crown upstairs."
"Miretooth won't be picking anyone else off the fen path. That fang belongs in a case, not a throat."
"Sir Edric can sleep now. The dead are back where they belong, and his signet is safe in the hall. Good job keeping your nerve when the air turned cold."
"You look steadier now. Let the toughest one take the first hit, let the sharpest one pick the target, and come back alive enough for supper."

courier_peep_marrow.text: "Message for the post, chalk mark for the route, errand for the person who forgot they had legs. That's me. If I look quick, it is because slow couriers learn where every puddle lives."

joss_veller.text: "Coilback-seven on a civic plate is not a ghost story. It is an old order still being obeyed after everyone with sense stopped signing work slips. That gives me a lever."

"The shard says the line is carrying orders. I need the clamp that held those orders to the stone. Check the causeway sockets, then the Sluice Walk. If the stamps match, this is a public work gone wrong, not a ghost with theatrical habits."

"There it is: Brambleford road-light stamp, maintenance number, ward groove. Ugly, but civic. The wrong light is obeying a rule after the people who wrote it stopped being available for corrections. That means the lock and lamp house can be forced to answer."
"The lamp house is the crown of the drowned line. If the thing inside calls up a ward, cut down whatever answered it first. The light will weaken once the support keeping it honest stops existing."

"Good. The line runs through the Sluice Walk and the Sunken Lock. Break enough of the drowned crew that the lamp house has to carry its own weight, then keep climbing while the light still thinks it has the initiative."
"The lock is broken and the south light has fewer places to lie. Follow it to the weir, confirm how it feeds the lamp house, and do not stand where the old glass is brightest."
"The Chain Keeper is not alive, not properly dead, and not interested in my categories. It sits in the Sunken Lock enforcing the old line. Break it and the lamp house loses its strongest hinge."
"The causeway pulse is real. Now chart Lantern Weir and the Sluice Walk, then bring me one clean shard of blackwater lensglass so I can measure the signal instead of guessing at it."

"The lower lanternworks under the observatory are old road-light machinery, not a miracle door. Reach the Drowned Causeway and bring me a live lamp coil. If it hums like a bad secret, that is the one."

"The south line is dark again. Properly dark, not hiding-current dark or waiting-for-a-better-word dark. I am going to write three reports, distrust two of them, and still admit the important part: the prism belongs upstairs where everyone can see what stopped humming."

"There. Hear that? The lower lanternworks are quiet enough to think in. The Trophy Hall upstairs has a place for the Blackwater Beacon Core because some wins ought to stay where the whole family can point at them."
"Every groove down here belongs to a road-light line Brambleford forgot it owned. The south groove woke up angry, and that is enough mystery without giving it a grander name."

"Most folk think I light lamps. True enough. They forget a town lantern is also a promise, a boundary, and sometimes a signal with civic handwriting. The brass remembers more than the flame does, and I prefer to measure what it remembers."

leda_thornwick.text: "Boots, cloaks, trail gear, fair trade. If it keeps weather off you or keeps your pack from betraying you, I have an opinion and a price. Usually in that order."

mayor_elric_thorne.text: "Pib sent the cellar count? Good. People like to call this sort of thing small until the wagons stop and the ledgers start telling the truth louder than the bells. Hand it here, then keep your boots ready for the East Gate."
"The inn stores are accounted for. That means we can make decisions instead of guesses, which is as close to luxury as a mayor gets before breakfast. The road still needs eyes."

"Then finish it. A wrong light in a drowned public works line is exactly the kind of sentence I would prefer to stop using. End the lamp house, come back alive, and I'll call that a proper frontier result."

"A drowned weir still running by bad intention alone is the sort of problem towns regret underestimating. Clear the lock line, prove the thing can be reached, and then end it before we have to start naming watch shifts after it."

"So the marsh was not merely growing a large predator. Fine. If Joss is right about the drowned weir, confirm it, map it, and tell me whether Brambleford needs to fear an old civic failure with a mean streak."
"Then finish Blackfen cleanly enough that the town can start saying south road again without sounding foolish. If the marsh truly has one ruling beast, bring that sentence to an end."
"Bandits, goblins, now the marsh edge. Every solved problem seems to uncover a less sociable one underneath it. Fine. Confirm what Blackfen is growing and make sure it stays south of our map."

"Then finish it. The ridge tower was built to keep trouble out, not to tax every honest wagon trying to reach Brambleford alive. Bring Blackreed down and we'll have one less ambitious problem on the map."
"The old tower is occupied, then. Good. Clear answers are easier to hate properly. Rowan knows the sort of fight this will become. Work with him and make the ridge expensive for bandits again."

"Brother Alden says the old knight has fully risen. Then finish it. Reach the Sunken Dais, end Sir Edric, and bring back whatever signet or proof he still clutches so I can tell the town this chapter is closed."

"So the causeway was not imagination. Good. I prefer confirmed bad news to rumors. Push on to the Barrow Circle, cut down the first dead things you find, and leave the chapel the harder question of why they woke."

"Our western lanterns are failing one by one, and the watch swears something moves around the old stones after dusk. Speak with Brother Alden at the chapel, then follow the old stone path to the barrow causeway and tell me whether this is fear or fact."

"The south line is dark. I can stop writing impossible phrases like active drowned civic threat in the margin of the town ledger. Put the prism in the hall, then rest before someone discovers a new category of expense."

"There. Hear that? The lower lanternworks are quiet enough to think in. The Trophy Hall upstairs has a place for the Blackwater Beacon Core because some wins ought to stay where the whole family can point at them."
"Blackreed is finished. The ridge standard is in the hall, and the road doesn't have a toll-taker with ambitions anymore. That is a civic victory, not just a tactical one."
"The warrens have stopped growing. Grubnak is done, and the road stores are where they belong. The Trophy Hall upstairs is looking better for it too."
"Miretooth is gone, and the fen edge is just mud and water again. Mira says the marsh remembers fear now. Good. Bring the proof to the hall upstairs so the town can see it."
"The old graves have settled. Edric is properly buried this time, and his signet is in the vitrine upstairs. That is a chapter closed that I never wanted to read twice."
"You've done enough on the southern trail that I trust your eyes. The chapel has been asking for steady boots, and the west lantern watch could use someone who doesn't startle easy."
"A mayor mostly counts damage, grain, and who still owes whom after the rain. Lately I have also been counting how many people think the old barrows are somebody else's problem."

mender_veska_flint.text: "Torren makes things meant to last. I make repairs meant to solve the next ugly problem before it solves you. If you want trapwork, clamp fixes, wire lashings, or something useful built out of what the road coughed up, use the workbench here."

"If you're hunting better mechanisms, keep your eyes open. Goblin hexers steal anything not nailed down, fence-cutters and ridge scouts lift ward notes off dead caravans, barrow lights cough old formula sheets back into the dark, and half the marsh returns my parts only after someone else bleeds for them. Study any pattern worth keeping."

mira_fenleaf.text: "That tally is ugly in the useful way. Ruk was counting cuts, rails, and wagon marks because the road was a plan to him, not a tantrum. Good. Now we can answer a plan with one of our own."
"Those reed tags moved without mud taking credit. That means the marsh is being handled, not merely haunted. I hate that distinction, but it tells us where to look next."

"The Reedflats tags should hold still unless water or hands move them. They are not holding still. Check them against Carrion Rise, then watch Boglight Hollow. If the lights move against the wind, the marsh is misreading the road for us."

"That map is worse than I hoped and better than guessing. The tags did not wander because the mud wanted a joke. Something east of the wallow is teaching the light to lie. Miretooth is still teeth first, but the route beyond him is the stranger answer."

"Good. These nails are all bent the same way, and the tally marks put the stolen rails moving toward Ruk's fire. That gives the repair crews a starting point and gives the mayor something better than worry to count."

"The drowned lamp house sits beyond the lock line at the far east of the weir. If the light shields itself with lesser things, cut them down first. What followed Miretooth this far isn't an animal anymore."

"The Sluice Walk and the Sunken Lock are the heart of it. Clear enough of the drowned crews that the lamp house has to show itself properly, then finish the climb with the whole party still breathing."

"Miretooth was guarding the edge, not causing it. Joss says the wrong light east of the wallow belongs to an old drowned weir. Go through the causeway and the lamp line and see what still thinks it has authority out there."
"Miretooth holds the far wallow where the water goes black and the reeds stop moving like wind. If he vanishes, don't spread out. He comes back for whoever looks easiest to finish."
"Push through the Reedflats and Carrion Rise. Kill enough Blackfen things that the trail stops feeling measured, and keep an eye on the bog lights. The wrong ones drift against the wind."

"South of Fencebreaker Camp the ground turns mean and wet fast. Take the Fenreach Track, then work east until you hit the hollow with the bad lights. That's the first sign the marsh is done pretending it is only mud."
"Grubnak sits east of the Feast Hall in the court he built out of lids, shields, and stolen road junk. Expect brutes first, hexers second, and a king mean enough to treat supper like strategy."
"Don't just sprint the warrens. Hit the Sludge Run, the midden, and the hall hard enough that the hexers stop sending anything organized back toward the road."
"East of Ruk's old camp the hill breaks open into a goblin sink cut. Take that breach, follow the smoke into the Torchgut tunnel, and see how far the road-cutters really run below us."

"Ruk's old camp is just the gate now. Push east along Goblin Road, north at the camp, then keep the tower wall on your left until you reach Blackreed's perch. If anyone looks shaky, he'll see it before you do."
"Bandits took the old ridge tower while everyone watched the woods and barrows. Go east from here, keep to Goblin Road until Fencebreaker Camp, then head north into the climb."
"The west side's the trouble now. Follow the old stone path through the woods until it opens onto the barrow causeway. If the dead are already walking, don't stand where the crows can measure you."
"Edric's dais sits past the barrow circle. If the chapel's right and he's wrapped in grave-light, cut down whatever answers his call before you try to finish him."
"Greymaw's hollow lies beyond the Briar Glade. If he vanishes into the brush, hold your nerve. He likes to lunge for anyone who looks ready to break."

"Ruk's camp is just beyond Wolf Turn. He has wagon paint on his chopping block and fence rails stacked like trophies. Bring your party, keep pressure on him when he bellows for help, and watch that axe."
"Goblin Road can breathe again, but the woods have gone strange. The trail starts just south of the gate. Watch for briar imps and the bigger wolf tracks, and check your enemies before you commit."

"The road crews need proof they can carry in a hand, not another story shouted over the gate. Check the Old Fence Line, pull together enough bent nails to show how the rails were stripped, then look at Ruk's camp before you bring me the pattern."

"The south edge is quieter now. The reed marks hold where I set them, the bad lights have stopped walking against the wind, and the marsh has gone back to being dangerous in honest ways. That is enough of a win for one frontier town."
"The marsh is mud and water again, not a sentence waiting to be finished. Miretooth is gone. Put the fang in the hall, then get some rest. You earned the silence."
"Goblin Road can breathe again, and Ruk's little kingdom is finished. Put the broken axe head upstairs. It is a better trophy than it was a tool."
"Start at the gate, then push to the Old Fence Line and Wolf Turn. Look for claw mud, knife cuts, and anything dragged from the cart. If trouble shows, size up your enemies before you fight."
"Goblins count. Wolves don't. Clear the cutters anywhere along Goblin Road and watch for stolen fence scrap in your pack. The pattern matters now."
"The road's quieter than it was. Not safe. Just quieter. Stay sharp and assume every bend is trying to embarrass you."

mistress_elira_thorne.text: "Technique is what survives after panic burns off. Practice gives it shape, discipline keeps it standard, and I correct the part you keep flattering. If you want to refine what you know, speak to me. If you want your whole focus back, I can break the pattern cleanly, but I do not do it for free."

quartermaster_nella_cobb.text: "Crate open, slate marked, inventory counted twice. Take the supply that keeps you prepared, bring back gear that can serve the next hand, and do not make me discover mystery pockets by sound."

ringhand_brask.text: "Rail marks the ring, timing teaches the fight, and a good lesson lands before my bark has to. Step in, keep your feet under you, and let the first mistake be useful instead of decorative."

sergeant_tamsin_vale.text: "Alarm means triage. Yard first, checklist second, command voice last because people hear panic before words. Stand where I put you, check what I name, and move when the road asks."

sister_maybelle.text: "The ribbon confirms it, then. The moonleaf is not afraid of the woods. It is leaning away from the barrows. I will send Alden the gentle version, which is still going to ruin his afternoon."

"Take this chalk and do not make it dramatic. Find the old stone path, copy the mark cleanly, and bring back a moonleaf sprig if the roots are still growing wrong around it. If the warning faces the barrows, I want to know before Alden has to pretend he is not worried."

"That mark is older than my herb notes and less comforting. It is not warning the woods away from us. It is warning us away from what waits past them. I will tell Alden gently, which means directly but with tea."

"If you have not settled your calling yet, do it before you go collecting scars for one that does not suit you. The chapel turns out capable paladins, the woods turn out capable druids, and both make themselves useful faster than boasters do."

"Brother Alden has taken over the chapel watch for now. If the mayor has you walking west, listen to the bell before you cross the barrows. It is never good when iron sounds tired. If you want the chapel at your back first, pray there before you go."
"The old graves have a way of holding onto duty too long. Brother Alden will know the rites. You bring the part that lands harder."

"Moonleaf likes cold shade and bad company. Check your pack as you go. Three sprigs keeps me in poultices for a little while, which means less harm turning into grief because someone waited too long."
"Whatever is wrong in the woods gathers around Greymaw. If he falls, the herbs may recover, the smaller things may remember fear, and I may stop running out of clean bandages before supper."
"The trail south of the gate used to be calmer than Goblin Road. Now the roots feel restless and even the moonleaf has started growing where it shouldn't."
"The moonleaf has stopped curling in on itself. That is the kind of good sign I trust more than speeches."
"The chapel lamps burned steady all morning. No cough in the flame, no chill under the door, no patient waiting in the glass. That is care too: trouble ended before it learns another name."
"Ruk is done, thank the lanterns. Now the woods need looking after. Speak to Mira, or head south if you've already decided trouble deserves a personal visit."

"If you insist on being heroic, at least try not to bleed on the floorboards. The town still needs hands steady enough to gather herbs, carry the wounded, and choose care before injury becomes a sermon."

torren_ironroot.text: "Forge is hot, anvil is clean, scrap goes in that bin unless it is lying about being useful. Bring metal, ask for repair, and do not tell me iron has a personality until it pays rent."

uncle_pib_underbough.text: "That is my flour mark wearing goblin sludge like a bad hat. If they are sorting stolen food under the road, they are not scavenging. They are supplying. I dislike the difference very much."

"If the goblins have a whole kitchen under the road, I would like to know whether it is eating my kitchen. Look through the midden and that feast hall of theirs. Bring back a label, a sack scrap, anything with a town mark on it. Preferably not the soup."

"That is my flour mark, and that is definitely not my gravy. Ruk was cutting the road, but something below him was planning dinner. Thank you. I hate being right with documentation, but it is useful. Food tells the truth when braggarts don't."

"Cellar is quiet, which is a blessing, but quiet flour sacks still need counting. Take this tally to Mayor Elric before the road gets any cleverer about being closed. Tell him the inn can feed worried people for now, but not if everyone starts eating like heroes."
"Good. Elric has the numbers, I have my cellar back, and the soup can stop being a strategic resource for at least one hour. That is what victory looks like when it wears an apron."

"I would love to say the bell scared the rats into good manners. It did not. They are chewing grain like the road might stay closed for a week, which is rude and strategically alarming because the stores matter now. Head down to the cellar, clear them out, then come back when the scratching stops."

"Good. The cellar's fit for flour again, which matters if wagons keep arriving in pieces. If you want your next bruise outdoors, Mira's waiting at the East Gate. Check your objectives if you want the road written plain before you go."
"You look chewed on. Sit down, eat something warm, and rest before you volunteer for another heroic misunderstanding."

"First days are for getting your bearings. If the town feels wide, check your objectives. If the road feels wider, come back here and rest. If you want something calmer, the wharf south of the green is open and the hearth here will take anything decent you catch."
"If the road has had enough of you for one evening, cook something honest and eat before you head back out. The Great Catch Log's right here too, if you feel like proving the river wrong."
"The inn's still safe ground. Patch up here, empty your pack if it rattles too much, then go bother something meaner than you. Or don't. Some evenings are for the wharf, the kettle, and supper."
